subject: Energy
title: Mini-Grids for Rural Power
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mini-Grids for Rural Power usable.

hook.text: Mini-grids serve communities too remote for the main grid—a local solar array with battery storage powers a village.

buildup.text: They can power homes, shops, clinics, and schools—enabling economic activity that kerosene lamps never could.

discovery.text: Smart meters and prepaid billing make mini-grids financially viable—customers pay for exactly what they use.

twist.text: When the national grid eventually arrives, mini-grids can integrate or compete—they're not a dead-end investment.

climax.text: The World Bank estimates 500 million people will be best served by mini-grids—a massive market taking shape.

punchline.text: One village, one solar array—mini-grids bring power locally.

quiz.question: How many people could mini-grids best serve according to the World Bank?
